fields.name: trigger

fields.name: window
fields.description: Wins over the manifest and module window.

operations.name: container
operations.description: Deterministic, idempotent upsert: the same (kind, key) always resolves to the same container id. Requires db.

operations.name: setMaxBackgroundAgents
operations.description: Floors the limit, clamps it to at least 1, uses 4 for non-finite input, and drains the background queue up to the new limit.

operations.name: dispose
operations.description: Clears the background queue, disposes child sessions, and settles every pending done promise so background handles never hang.

operations.name: registry
operations.description: The validated agent registry (see The Registry).

operations.name: doctor
operations.description: Flushes pending trace writes, then checks trace invariants. Requires db.

operations.name: readApiService
operations.description: Lazily created; flushes the trace writer before each read. Backs createKernelTraceReadApi. Requires db.

operations.name: catalogApiService
operations.description: Backs createKernelCatalogApi: agent listing, detail, prompt saves, and revision history.

fields.name: allowWrites
fields.description: Default false. Prompt saves write catalog files on disk, so enable only in dev; a read-only service answers the save route with 403.

operations.name: agentManager
operations.description: Subagent manager over this kernel's spawn pipeline (see Subagents).

text.insert: An agent is a directory discovered by its
manifest: a prompt plus optional context, tools, and state sidecars that mirror the request sections.
defines the bundle file tree, the manifest, and the prompt document.

The manifest is pure data. There is no code entry point and no Markdown/frontmatter path; the manifest file itself is the registry entry, JSON-Schema validated. Spawning is granted per tool, not by a manifest flag (D77).

) and the source of truth. The registry validates it, renders it to XML-tagged Markdown, and computes its content hash (
over the canonical bytes). The rendered markdown beside it is a committed
snapshot (never hand-edited, never parsed by the registry), so PR diffs show the behavioral contract in the format the model receives.
The registry turns the catalog into validated runtime definitions.

Each bundle normalizes into a parsed agent: config, rendered prompt body, and

Registry boot fails with an aggregate of per-agent errors: unparseable manifests or prompts, prompt validation errors, variable drift, unknown tool profiles, spawner tools naming agents missing from the catalog (D77), name collisions, malformed sidecar exports. steps.text: Spawn one catalog agent
`Host` calls `kernel.spawnAgent(name, prompt, ctx, opts)`
The kernel reloads a changed `prompt.json`, resolves `opts.variant` and model aliases, and merges config defaults into `opts`.
Resolve run identity
Take the working directory from `opts.workingDir`, else `ctx.cwd`
Require `containerId` from `opts` or the parent `RunContext`
Pick the trigger: `opts.trigger`, else `parent-tool` with a `parentToolUseId`, else `operator`
Mint the `runId`
Resolve the agent
Render the static system prompt with resolved variables
Build one `SpawnContext` for the context loaders and the state seed
Create the state extension when the bundle activates one
Otherwise nothing registers and the session stays pass-through.
Create the Pi session
Build or reuse a Pi session manager
Load shared and private tool factories
Spawner tools bind their `dispatch` handle to the `AgentManager` here.
Create the Pi `AgentSession` with the session-binding marker
The marker always carries `containerId` and `runId`.
Pre-insert the session row and the agent-run row
The session row stamps `prompt_hash` and the resolved model; the run row stamps the trigger.
Attach the kernel emitter and usage recorder
Emitter emits `agent_session_start`
Attach the request-snapshot recorder unless `captureRequestSnapshots` is false
Emit `system_prompt_resolved` with `prompt_hash`
Build context when a resolver exists and the session has none
Emit `context_build_started`
Emit `context_input_resolved` once per loader
Emit `context_build_completed`
Add the result to the context set, or inject it into the transcript when pass-through
Subscribe to session events for streaming and the turn limit
Build `RunContext`
Emit `agent_run_start`
Trigger the Pi turn inside the run context
Emitter emits `pi_agent_start`, then `pi_turn_start` and `pi_turn_end` per turn
Emitter emits `user_message`, `assistant_message`, `tool_call_start`, and `tool_call_end`
Recorder emits one `pi_request_snapshot` per turn
Emitter emits `pi_agent_end`
An assistant `stopReason` of `error` fails the run.
Close the run on success
Settle the emitter, then flush the snapshot recorder and the state sink
Emit `agent_run_end` with status `ok` and run usage
Fold run usage into the session and container rollups
Write run status with the outbound event, and session status `ended`
Run status is `turn-limit` when the turn limit hit, `aborted` when the run or signal aborted, else `done`.
Close the run on failure
Settle the emitter, then flush the snapshot recorder and the state sink
Emit `agent_run_end` with status `error` and the error message
Fold usage observed before the failure into the rollups
Write run status `aborted` if the signal aborted, else `error`
Session status becomes `error`.
Rethrow the error to the caller

text.insert: Spawning is granted per tool, not per agent (D77): a
sidecar declares a spawner tool with an explicit
is the loud general opt-in), and the kernel injects a scoped
handle at session build time. There is no agent-level spawn permission flag, and the generic Pi subagent tools are disallowed for every kernel agent.
The dispatch handle enforces the allowlist, validates the target exists in the catalog (a wildcard spawner cannot turn a typo into a silently errored record), and auto-forwards

, and run-context identity. These values are captured at dispatch time and passed explicitly, so a queued background spawn keeps its own parent's identity no matter when, or from whose async context, the queue drains. The tool author cannot get these wrong.

The subagent manager coordinates foreground and background agent runs inside an active parent run. Foreground dispatch awaits completion and resolves with the agent record. Background dispatch resolves immediately with a handle whose

promise always exists and resolves with the final record when the child actually completes, including queued children, which have no record promise until they start, and queued children aborted before starting. Background work enters a FIFO queue when the concurrency limit (default 4, adjustable on the kernel instance) is reached. The manager also owns abort and stop behavior, result delivery, parent-to-child Pi session link markers, and

Callers can steer a subagent before its session exists: the manager stores steering messages and flushes them once the session is created. Steering is a control action, so it is observable. Each steering message emits exactly one
for a held message; queued emissions wait for the run's trace identity and flush with it.
Subagent execution re-enters the same spawn path with inherited identity: the parent's
trigger. Primary agents and subagents share the same runtime contracts.
